title: Physically-based elevation and compact type rebaseline for dense tables
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Dense tables and datagrids across the console suffer from inconsistent elevation/shadow heuristics and cramped typographic rhythm. Multiple teams have added ad-hoc shadows and reduced font sizes, which leads to contrast regressions, visual noise, and unpredictable token overrides in CSS variables.

Goal: Introduce a physically-based elevation model (PBE) to replace legacy shadow maps, and rebaseline a compact typography token set specifically tuned for dense data surfaces (tables, charts toolbars, compact cards). Deliverables: token definitions, Figma updates, component patches, migration guide, visual regression suite, and a staged rollout plan with feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: A single tokenized elevation system (pbe-elevation-0..6) maps consistently to shadow offset/blur/opacity on supported platforms (web, electron).
Compact typography tokens (type-compact-xxx) defined for 3 density breakpoints and validated for numeric legibility at 12–13px equivalents.
All table and datagrid components consume new tokens and pass visual-regression baseline (threshold <= 2% pixel diff for approved variants).
Migration tooling (token alias layer) present so older CSS vars resolve to new tokens with no runtime visual regressions for 95% of pages.
Design review sign-off from PM and Accessibility (contrast checks, focus ring visible at compact density).
Release plan documented and gated by opt-in feature flag for Dedicated customers before full rollout.
tasks: Audit existing shadow tokens and component overrides across console (identify custom styles and inline shadows).
Define PBE token spec with numerical parameters: elevation distance, umbra/penumbra blur, alpha curves; include visual samples.
Create compact type token set: font-size, line-height, letter-spacing, numeric tabular-nums setting, and token aliases.
Update Figma library with new tokens, create contrast & density canvases for designers and infra.
Prototype CSS vars and runtime alias layer for backward compatibility (token aliases v1).
Implement component changes in Button, Table, Datagrid, Card, Chart-legend (React + CSS-in-JS).
Run visual regression tests and fix outliers (threshold tuning and selective exceptions).
Write migration guide for product teams and eng (breaking changes, opt-out instructions).
Ship behind feature flag, monitor telemetry for UI anomalies and accessibility complaints.
comments: 2026-03-10 Ava Patel: Initial ticket created after cross-team review (Console UX sync). Noticed multiple one-off shadows in analytics and sales dashboards. Proposing a more physical model to reduce token sprawl.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Engineering scoped impact — estimated 3–5 frontend modules to update. Will add ENG dependency once we finalize token spec. Asking for a clear mapping table between legacy shadows and PBE elevations.

2026-03-12 Diego Morales (Accessibility): Quick checks: compact numeric type must use tabular-nums and maintain 4.5:1 for body text or provide compensating contrast tokens. Flagging potential need for slightly heavier weights on dense numeric displays.

2026-03-12 Design review: Decided to cap elevation levels to 0..6 and map to z-distance values that produce consistent ambient/point light ratios. Agreement to avoid per-component bespoke elevations except for experimental components behind flags.

2026-03-13 Engineering comment (ENG-98765): Linked eng ticket created for migration work and rollout orchestration. Initial alias shim implemented in prototype branch. Performance note: avoid multiple box-shadows when possible; prefer single-shadow with composite opacity.
decisions: Adopt a 0..6 PBE elevation scale, where elevation-0 is flat and elevation-6 is the strongest (approx 24px z distance).
Shadow implementation: single-layer shadow for most components (optimized blur + offset + alpha), reserve dual-layer only for edge cases like floating modals),
Compact typography baseline: three tokens (compact-sm 12px, compact-md 13px, compact-lg 14px) with explicit line-height tokens and enforced tabular-nums for numeric-heavy cells.
Token rollout via aliasing: legacy tokens (shadow-xx) will map to pbe-elevation-yy for 3 release cycles before deprecation.
notes: This ticket should be coordinated with the Dedicated rollout calendar. Engineering requested a small perf budget to reduce multi-shadow overhead; include perf regression benchmarks in the visual regression pipeline.
